sectionC.title: MCP PROTOCOL — AI AUTONOMY LAYER
sectionC.subtitle: 59 custom tools (and counting) across multiple servers exposed to all AI CLIs — plus custom MCP server support
sectionC.intro: Sciorex exposes 59 custom tools to every connected CLI via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Every subsystem—PDFs, library, tickets, flows, agents, secrets—is accessible to whichever CLI you use. This means Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or any other connected CLI can autonomously annotate a PDF, add it to your library, create a ticket to review its findings, and trigger a workflow to compile your LaTeX document—all from a single natural language instruction. You can also add your own MCP servers (Playwright, database connectors, custom tools) and Sciorex will automatically expose them to all CLIs.

tools: pdf_read — Extract text from PDFs by page range
pdf_get_annotations — Retrieve all annotations from a PDF
latex_get_errors — Retrieve compilation errors and warnings
sciorex_create_ticket — Create with type, priority, subtasks
sciorex_change_status — Move tickets through workflow stages
+ get, update, list, subtask CRUD, epic CRUD, unlink
+ list, get, delete for agents and flows
request_secret — Access secrets (value never exposed to AI)

sectionD.title: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
sectionD.subtitle: 9 entries — vibe kanban, worktrees, MCP, privacy & more

faq.q: What is vibe kanban and how does Sciorex implement it?
faq.a: Vibe kanban is a workflow where AI agents execute tasks in parallel while you focus on planning, review, and strategic oversight. Sciorex is the original vibe kanban platform—each agent operates in its own git worktree (isolated branch + working directory), so agents never produce merge conflicts. You review each agent’s changes through a built-in diff tool, approve or reject, then merge. The kanban board tracks which tasks are queued, in progress, or done.

Yes. Completely free for personal and professional use—no subscriptions, no premium tiers, no feature gates. Sciorex is a wrapper around existing AI CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, LM Studio, Ollama). You install the CLI you want to use, and Sciorex orchestrates it. Your costs are whatever the CLI charges—or zero with fully local models via LM Studio/Ollama.

faq.q: How is Sciorex different from Cursor or Windsurf?
faq.a: Cursor and Windsurf are AI-enhanced code editors. Sciorex is a development platform that wraps your existing AI CLIs and adds orchestration on top: visual workflows (drag-and-drop flow builder with 9 node types), parallel agent execution via git worktrees, kanban project management, MCP tool exposure (59 custom tools available to all CLIs plus custom MCP server support), council mode with custom personas for multi-LLM debate, an embedded VS Code Server for full IDE experience, a community marketplace for sharing agents/flows/personas/templates, and a research suite (LaTeX, PDF, reference library). You install the CLI you want (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, etc.) and Sciorex handles the rest—100% local control.

faq.q: How do worktrees work with parallel agents?
faq.a: Each git worktree is a separate branch checked out in its own directory with an independent AI session. You can spin up multiple worktrees from the UI, assign each one a task (manually or via kanban), and let agents work simultaneously—one implementing a feature, another writing tests, a third refactoring. Since each worktree has its own working directory, there are no file conflicts. Worktree merging with built-in conflict detection handles reconciliation when you’re ready.

faq.q: What is MCP and what does it mean for my workflow?
faq.a: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI models call structured tools. Sciorex exposes 59 custom tools (and counting) across multiple servers: Research (16 tools for PDF read/annotate, LaTeX compile, library management), Tickets (23 tools for ticket CRUD, subtasks, epics, blockers, comments, resource linking), Resources (11 tools for agent and flow management), Interactions (4 tools for user communication), and Secrets (4 tools for credential management). Every CLI you install—Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode—automatically gets access to all tools. You can also add your own custom MCP servers (Playwright, database connectors, etc.) and Sciorex exposes them to all CLIs.

faq.q: Does Sciorex support the ralph loop technique?
faq.a: Yes. The ralph loop (Ralph Wiggum loop) is an iterative pattern where agents continuously work on tasks with progress persisting in git history rather than context windows. Sciorex’s worktree isolation, session forking, and flow engine (with loop/condition nodes) make it ideal for long-running agentic sessions. You can also set up scheduled flow triggers for fully automated iteration cycles.

Sciorex wraps 6 AI CLIs: Claude Code (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5), Gemini CLI (Gemini 3 Flash, Pro), OpenAI Codex CLI (GPT-5.3 Codex), OpenCode, LM Studio, and Ollama (Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen, etc.). Install any CLI you want to use, and Sciorex detects and integrates it automatically. Council mode can mix CLIs—e.g., Claude Code debating Gemini CLI debating Codex—in structured rounds with custom personas (YAML import/export). Extended Thinking (Think / Think Hard / Think Harder / Ultrathink) controls reasoning depth per message.

faq.q: Where is my data stored? Is Sciorex private?
faq.a: Everything runs and stays on your local machine—100% of it. No telemetry, no analytics, no cloud sync. Projects are plain folders—git init when you want version control, then push to GitHub, GitLab, or any remote for free backup. Secrets (tokens, credentials) are stored in an encrypted local vault and never exposed to AI models (the Secrets MCP server handles access control with user approval). The only network traffic is between the CLI and its provider when you initiate a chat. You can go fully offline with local models via LM Studio or Ollama.

faq.q: Can I extend Sciorex with custom agents and workflows?
faq.a: Yes. Custom agents are defined with a system prompt, model selection, tool permissions, and execution sandboxing. Council personas let you shape how each AI participates in multi-model debates (with YAML import/export). Workflows use a visual flow builder with 9 node types (Trigger, Agent, Condition, Wait, Parallel, Merge, Transform) and support breakpoints, step-through debugging, and I/O inspection. You can also add custom MCP servers—any MCP-compatible tool (Playwright, database connectors, etc.) gets automatically exposed to all CLIs. Everything—agents, flows, personas, LaTeX templates—can be shared via the community marketplace.
